docRequirement: errors.md:1435-1452 ("### Memory index is over its read limit") binds a WRITE to the auto-memory index `MEMORY.md` that leaves it over either read limit — 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first — to return an error to Claude AFTER the write ("Claude Code delivers the error to Claude after the write rather than printing it as a banner in your terminal"), naming the actual line count, the limit crossed, that the write succeeded, that "everything past the limit is silently dropped each time the index is loaded", and the remedy "Rewrite it to under 140 lines now: keep one line per entry, move detail into topic files, and merge or drop stale entries." Two refinements are part of the contract: measurement counts only the content that loads — "YAML frontmatter and block-level HTML comments are stripped before the index is loaded, so they're excluded from the measurement" (:1443) — and "When Claude's write brings the file near a limit without crossing it, Claude Code returns a milder reminder to compact the index instead of this error." (:1447)
current: No write-time measurement and no model-facing signal exist on either memory writer. (1) The model-facing `remember` tool: `appendMemory` (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:39-49) reads the existing file, formats the entry, writes a temp file, renames and chmods — it measures nothing and returns `void`; `handleRemember` then does `appendMemory(filePath, memory)` and `return successResponse(`Saved memory to ${filePath}`)` (:90-91), which is the only thing the model ever sees. The tool is live and model-reachable (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:981, `safeMode: 'block'`), and `successResponse` (packages/session-tools-core/src/response.ts:13-19) carries only that one text block. (2) A SECOND writer on the renderer path has the same shape: `appendMemoryFile` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:122-132), reached from `appendMemoryForSession` (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:48-88, call at :80, dispatched at :564-565), whose `MemoryAppendResult` is `{ success, scope, error? }` only (packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:438-442) and whose UI shows an unconditional success toast (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/ChatDisplay.tsx:1552-1575). (3) The limits such an error would name are themselves not the documented pair: `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8) is applied only as a silent slice inside `readMemoryFile` — `readFileSync(filePath,'utf-8').split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` (:31) — and there is NO byte limit anywhere on the memory path; the subsystem's only byte constant is `AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024` (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-cleanup.ts:33), a skip-guard for the scheduled dream pass (:125), not a load or write cap. (4) There are TWO load paths and the cap is on the dormant one: `getSystemPrompt` calls `loadMemoryPromptBlock` — the sole route to that 200-line slice (memory-store.ts:317-334, via `readMemoryFileWithImports` :66-110) — only when `capabilityContextPinned` is false (packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:412 declares the flag, :453-455 gates on it); on the live capability-runtime path `composePinnedCapabilityContext` reads each memory layer with `await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource)` (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:976-977), and that `readText` returns the whole file (packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts:169-186 — `readFileSync`, hash/revision check, `content.toString('utf-8')`), the only content ever removed being `@import` lines (base-agent.ts:1003-1007). (5) No frontmatter or block-level-HTML-comment exclusion from any measurement exists: `stripAutoMemoryMarkers` (memory-store.ts:159-163) removes only the inline `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` marker, and on the legacy path it runs inside `mergeMemoryContents` (:165-183) AFTER the :31 slice. Absence positively controlled with NUL-safe grep: `grep -rnaiE "read limit|over its |25 ?kb|rewrite it to under|compact the index|memory index" packages apps --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx` returns no memory-related hit.
divergence: The whole write-time mechanism is absent — not misnamed, not narrower. Nothing measures the index after a write, so neither documented output exists: not the hard over-limit error, and not the milder near-limit reminder. Both writers return a bare unconditional success (`Saved memory to <path>` for the model; `{success:true,scope}` for the UI). Secondary deltas that make the doc's error text untrue until they are fixed too: the 25KB byte limit does not exist at all; the 200-line limit exists only as a silent slice on the LEGACY composer and is entirely absent on the live capability path, so on the default path nothing is dropped (the whole oversized index is pinned every turn instead); and the measurement's documented exclusion of YAML frontmatter and block-level HTML comments has no implementation. The pre-v2.1.210 behaviour the page names as the defect ("an over-limit index was silently truncated on the next load with no write-time signal") is exactly what the legacy path does today.

change.what: Add `export const MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT = 25 * 1024;` next to MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT (:8). Add `export function measureLoadedMemory(content: string): { lines: number; bytes: number }` that FIRST strips a leading YAML frontmatter fence and every block-level HTML comment (a `<!-- ... -->` span occupying whole lines) and only then counts lines and `Buffer.byteLength(...,'utf8')` — it must NOT strip the inline trailing `<!-- nessy:auto:DATE -->` marker, which is not block-level and therefore still counts. Add `export function memoryIndexOverflowMessage(filePath, measured)` emitting the doc's text verbatim in shape (`Error: this write left the memory index at <path> at <N> lines, over its 200-line read limit. The write succeeded, but everything past the limit is silently dropped each time the index is loaded — entries at the end are already invisible to readers. Rewrite it to under 140 lines now: keep one line per entry, move detail into topic files, and merge or drop stale entries.`), with the byte-limit wording as the sibling branch, and `export function memoryIndexNearLimitMessage(...)` for the milder compact-the-index reminder plus a named near-limit threshold constant. Apply MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT inside `readMemoryFile` (:29-33) alongside the existing line slice so the error's "silently dropped" claim is true on the legacy path.

Make `appendMemory` (:39-49) return the content it wrote (or have `handleRemember` re-read the file), measure it, and at :90-91 return the overflow text appended to the existing `Saved memory to <path>` success when a limit is crossed, or the milder reminder when the write lands near a limit — still a success result, because the doc says the write succeeded and the error is delivered after it. This package deliberately has NO dependency on `@nessy-agent/shared` (stated at packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:939), so the limits, `measureLoadedMemory` and the two message builders must be duplicated locally with the same keep-in-sync comment the file already uses for `MEMORY_FILE_NAME` (:12) and `AUTO_MEMORY_MARKER_RE` (:14-21). Not a one-liner: measurement + two message branches.

Apply the same 200-line / 25KB cap to each `runtime.view.memory` layer body read at :976-977 before it is pushed into `bodies` (:1014), so the live capability path actually truncates what the write-time error says is dropped. Without this the error is factually wrong on the default path. Shared work with f092/f098/f104 (the missing 25KB load cap) — one implementation closes all of them.

After `appendMemoryFile(filePath, memory)` (:80), measure the written file and return the overflow/near-limit text on a new additive `warning?: string` field so the UI writer surfaces the same condition the tool path does. Consistency half of the fix, not the doc's own requirement (the doc's error is model-facing).

Add optional `warning?: string` to the interface at :438-442, and surface it as a distinct toast in apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/ChatDisplay.tsx:1560-1570 (`handleSaveToMemory`). Additive-only, but it crosses the RPC/IPC wire — see blastRadius.

Two cases: measurement excludes YAML frontmatter and a block-level HTML comment while still counting the inline `<!-- nessy:auto:DATE -->` marker; `readMemoryFile` truncates a >25KB file whose line count is under 200 (the whichever-comes-first branch).

No test file exists for this handler today (codegraph reports no covering tests for `appendMemory`). Add one positive and one negative: a write that leaves the index at 214 lines returns the overflow text in the tool result; a small write returns the plain `Saved memory to <path>` unchanged.

blastRadius: `readMemoryFile` (memory-store.ts:29) has two production consumers: `readMemoryFileWithImports` (:77) and packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:427, which walks its lines to DISCOVER `@import` topic files. Adding a byte cap there changes which imports a large index yields, and therefore the capability record set (keys, revisions, content hashes) built at native-sources.ts:405-435 — that is a capability-snapshot/generation effect, not just a prompt effect, so the cap belongs on a named parameter rather than silently on the shared default. `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (:317) has 3 callers in packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts and is covered by packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts and packages/shared/src/prompts/__tests__/system.test.ts. `appendMemoryFile` (:122) has 4 call sites in packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts, covered by packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.memory.test.ts. The `remember` tool is registered at packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:981, so a changed result string is model-facing on every backend that mounts session tools (Pi, Claude, Codex). `composePinnedCapabilityContext` has no covering tests today. WIRE BOUNDARY, stated explicitly: `MemoryAppendResult` travels shared/protocol/dto.ts -> apps/electron/src/shared/types.ts:343,401 -> ChatDisplay.tsx:1560, so the `warning?` field is an additive RPC/IPC schema change and a risk trigger under this repo's policy; the two other halves (measurement + tool-result text) cross no wire. No persistence-format change: MEMORY.md bytes on disk are untouched, only measured.
userImpact: Today nothing ever tells a user their memory index has outgrown its read limit. On the legacy (non-pinned-capability) composer every line past 200 stops reaching the model — the user keeps saying "remember this", the tool answers `Saved memory to …/MEMORY.md` every single time, and the oldest entries are already invisible with no signal anywhere. On the live capability-runtime path the failure inverts: no cap is applied at all, so an oversized index is pinned into EVERY turn and silently eats context budget instead. The observable surface is identical in both cases — an unconditional success in the tool result, an unconditional "memory saved" toast on the Save-to-memory UI path (ChatDisplay.tsx:1567), and never a prompt to compact the index. It surfaces the moment an index passes ~200 lines or ~25KB; a small index (this repo's own is well under) shows nothing, which is why the gap is easy to miss.
